 The horror genre appeals to millions of fans across the world for the escape it provides from the regular horrors of life. There’s a community feeling in watching a horror movie, whether you are collectively gasping in your living room or, better still, having a jump-scare in a theater full of people. The horrors are shared, be it psychological, body horror , or an axe-wielding serial killer hunting the final girl. We are days away from Halloween and horror fans are checking out their favorite flicks, old or new. Thrillers like David Fincher ’s Seven and Zodiac always bring fans back to the psychological horrors, while classics like Jonathan Demme ’s The Silence of the Lambs , Stanley Kubrick ’s The Shining, and such are back on streaming and PVOD charts. This year’s breakout horror flick Curry Barker ’s Obsession , A24’s Backrooms , Nia DaCosta ’s 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple , and more have fans’ attention as well.

 Among such titles that instill fear in its audience is the Evil Dead franchise. Started by Sam Raimi as an indie project, it has spawned a whole franchise that is haunting fans for over four decades. The latest installment, Evil Dead Burn , follows Alice Price ( Souheila Yacoub ), a young woman trapped in an abusive relationship with her husband, Will. When Will dies suddenly, Alice seeks closure by visiting her estranged, hostile in-laws at their secluded family vacation home. Soon, the trip turns into a nightmare as the discovery of a Necronomicon variant and a Kandarian Dagger accidentally unleashes a demonic force. One by one, the judgmental and abusive family members are possessed by Deadites , turning their intimate psychological flaws against Alice. Alice is forced into a brutal fight for survival and to end the generational trauma.

 Collider · Quiz 
 Collider Exclusive · 8 Questions · 2 Minutes 
 What Is Your Biggest Horror Nightmare ? 
 Elm Street · Chucky · Scream · The Conjuring 
 Four horror franchises. Four completely different ways of scaring you. One waits until you fall asleep. One makes sure nobody believes you. One is already in your group of friends. And one is in the house with your family. Answer eight quick questions about how you actually watch horror, and find out which nightmare was built for you. 
 😴 Elm Street (Freddy Krueger) 
 🧸 Chucky (Child's Play) 
 📞 Scream (Ghostface) 
 🕯️ The Conjuring (The Warren Files) 
 FIND YOUR NIGHTMARE → 
 QUESTION 1 / 8 THE SCENE 
 01 
 Which horror scene makes you cover your eyes? 
 Four classic images. One of them is worse than the others for you. 
 A Somebody falling asleep when they really should not. 
 B A toy that has moved, and nobody touched it. 
 C A phone ringing in an empty house. 
 D A child talking to somebody who is not there. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 2 / 8 THE NOISE 
 02 
 You are home alone and you hear a noise. First thought? 
 Everybody has one. It arrives before you have decided anything. 
 A I am exhausted and my mind is playing tricks on me. 
 B Something in this room is not where I left it. 
 C Somebody is in here with me. 
 D This house has never felt entirely right. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 3 / 8 THE RULE 
 03 
 Which horror movie rule would you break first? 
 Everybody thinks they would survive. Almost nobody actually does. 
 A Never fall asleep. 
 B Never leave it out of your sight. 
 C Never answer the phone. 
 D Never go down to the basement. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 4 / 8 THE REACTION 
 04 
 Something genuinely frightening happens. What do you do? 
 Not in a film. In your actual living room, tonight. 
 A Convince myself I imagined the whole thing. 
 B Tell someone, and brace for them not believing me. 
 C Work out which person I know could be behind it. 
 D Get everybody in the house into one room. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 5 / 8 MOVIE NIGHT 
 05 
 How do you actually watch a horror film? 
 Be honest about this one. Nobody is checking. 
 A Fine during. Wide awake at two in the morning. 
 B Shouting at the screen that nobody is listening. 
 C Calling the twist out loud before it lands. 
 D Through my fingers, holding on to something. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 6 / 8 THE DARE 
 06 
 Somebody offers you serious money. Which do you still refuse? 
 The amount does not matter. There is one on this list you are not doing. 
 A Fall asleep in a room I have never been in before. 
 B Keep an old doll on the shelf facing my bed. 
 C Answer every unknown number that calls after midnight. 
 D Spend one night alone in a house with a history. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 7 / 8 AFTER 
 07 
 Which feeling stays with you a week after the film? 
 Good horror does not stop when the credits do. 
 A Not wanting to turn the bedroom light off. 
 B Not trusting one particular object in my house. 
 C Looking twice at people I have known for years. 
 D Feeling like something came home with me. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 8 / 8 THREE A.M. 
 08 
 Something wakes you at 3am. What is the worst possibility? 
 Eight questions in, this is the one that decides your nightmare. 
 A That I am still asleep, and it knows it. 
 B That the thing nobody believed me about is here. 
 C That somebody with a key is downstairs. 
 D That something is in the doorway, watching us sleep. 
 REVEAL MY NIGHTMARE → 
 The Lights Just Went Out 
 Your Nightmare Is… 
 Four franchises, four completely different ways of getting underneath
 your skin. This is the one built out of your particular fear, why it works so well on you, and what
 it would leave behind.
 A Nightmare on Elm Street · Since 1984 
 Elm Street 
 Your nightmare does not wait outside the door. It waits for you
 to close your eyes, which you are going to have to do eventually, because nobody has ever
 won that particular argument.
 Freddy is horror's cruellest idea: a threat that lives in the one place you cannot
 guard, cannot lock, and cannot avoid forever.
 You are the one who is fine during the film and wide awake at two in the morning. Your
 own head is where this does its damage.
 These films understood exhaustion as a horror engine. The kids on Elm Street do not lose
 because they are weak. They lose because they are tired.
 You can lock every door in the house. You still have to sleep.
 Child's Play · Chucky · Since 1988 
 Chucky 
 Your nightmare is not really the doll. It is the face of the
 person you tell, and the way they decide, very kindly, that you have imagined all of it.
 Chucky works precisely because he is absurd. That is the trap: the more accurately you
 describe him, the less anybody is going to believe you.
 You are the one shouting at the screen because the characters are not listening. You
 know that feeling from real life too.
 The franchise is at its best when the adults in the room are the real obstacle, and you
 have met those adults.
 By the time somebody finally believes you, you will have handled most of it on your own.
 Scream · Ghostface · Since 1996 
 Scream 
 Your nightmare has your number, knows your name, and has almost
 certainly been inside your house before. The worst part is that you already know them.
 Scream is the only one of these where the killer takes the mask off and turns out to be
 somebody who was at the party.
 You are the person who calls the twist out loud before it lands. You watch people the
 same way you watch films.
 The franchise made the rules of horror part of the plot, which means the survivors are
 the ones paying attention. You would be paying attention.
 Everybody is a suspect, including the person who just offered to walk you home.
 The Conjuring · The Warren Files · Since 2013 
 The Conjuring 
 Your nightmare is not really about you. It is about the people
 asleep down the hall, and the feeling that whatever is here is not interested in leaving.
 The Conjuring films are domestic horror. The house, the family, the perfectly ordinary
 room that quietly stops feeling ordinary.
 Your instinct is to get everybody into one room. Your fear is protective rather than
 personal, which is rarer than it sounds.
 This is the one franchise where belief is the weapon. The people who come through it are
 the ones who are not alone and refuse to be.
 Whatever is here did not come for you. It came for the household, and you are the one
 standing in the hallway.

 'Evil Dead Burn' Is Hot on Streaming
 Directed by Sébastien Vaniček and co-written by Florent Bernard , the feature brilliantly touches upon the themes of grief and regret , domestic abuse and trauma, and overcoming toxic family dynamics. Vaniček’s kinetic, stylish direction coupled with film's visceral, relentless practical effects make it a standout in the franchise. It garnered a 70% Rotten Tomatoes rating from critics while an equally impressed audience gave it a 74% rating.
 Evil Dead Burn has taken over multiple streaming services, topping the charts of Amazon , HBO Max , and Netflix , as per FlixPatrol. Further, on the Apple TV Store, it has spent over 75 days on the charts, while on Amazon it has spent 79 days.
